name: Hvar
tagline: Croatia's glamorous lavender island, a car-free medieval harbour town backed by a hilltop fortress and a scatter of pine-covered islets offshore.
highlight: Watching the sun set from Fortica's ramparts, Hvar Town's terracotta rooftops and the Pakleni Islands glowing below.
shortDescription: Croatia's glamorous lavender island, a medieval harbour town backed by a hilltop fortress, with the pine-covered Pakleni Islands scattered just offshore.
metaDescription: A Hvar travel guide: Fortica Španjola, St Stephen's Square, the Pakleni Islands, lavender fields, food and how to plan a Dalmatian island trip.
nearestAirport: Split Airport (SPU), then a ferry or catamaran to Hvar
knownFor: Hvar Town, the Pakleni Islands, lavender fields
budget: €130–280 per day, mid-range to upscale (higher in peak summer)

image.alt: Hvar Town and St Stephen's Square

intro: Hvar is genuinely Croatia's most glamorous island, a sun-drenched strip of the Adriatic known for lavender fields, Venetian architecture and a harbour town that fills up with yachts every summer.
Its centrepiece is genuinely Hvar Town, a car-free medieval port overlooked by the hilltop Fortica fortress and framed by the pine-covered Pakleni Islands just offshore.

Beyond the harbour's nightlife, the island is genuinely also one of Croatia's sunniest and most fertile, its interior still scented with lavender and planted with some of the country's best vineyards.

whyVisit.intro: Hvar's case rests genuinely on combining postcard Dalmatian scenery with a genuinely lively, sociable atmosphere.

points.title: Hvar Town is genuinely one of Croatia's most beautiful harbours
points.text: A car-free medieval port town backed by a hilltop fortress.

points.title: The Pakleni Islands are genuinely a short boat ride away
points.text: Pine-covered islets with clear water and quiet coves, right offshore from the main harbour.

points.title: It's genuinely one of Europe's sunniest islands
points.text: Among the highest annual sunshine counts anywhere on the continent.

points.title: The lavender and wine are genuinely real, not just marketing
points.text: A fertile interior producing both alongside the coast's beach-club scene.

points.title: It works genuinely well for every kind of traveller
points.text: Lively harbourfront nightlife alongside quiet coves and hiking trails, depending on what you're after.

attractionsIntro: Hvar's essential sights are genuinely spread between its harbour town, hilltop fortress and the islands offshore.

attractions.name: Hvar Town's harbour
attractions.text: Genuinely the island's social heart, a car-free medieval port lined with cafés, yachts and Venetian-era architecture.
attractions.tip: Genuinely arrive by late afternoon for the harbour at its liveliest, golden-hour best.

attractions.name: Fortica Španjola

image.alt: Fortica Španjola, the fortress above Hvar Town

attractions.text: Genuinely the best view on the island, a 16th-century fortress on the hill directly above Hvar Town.
attractions.tip: Genuinely time the climb for sunset — the view over the town and Pakleni Islands is genuinely spectacular.

attractions.name: St Stephen's Square and Cathedral

image.file: File:St. Stephen Square and the Cathedral of St. Stephen (5969989950).jpg
image.alt: St Stephen's Square and Cathedral in Hvar Town

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the largest and oldest squares in Dalmatia, ringed by the town's baroque cathedral and arsenal.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a lovely spot for an evening coffee once the day's heat has faded.

attractions.name: The Pakleni Islands
attractions.text: Genuinely a scatter of pine-covered islets just offshore, with quiet coves and clear water a world away from the harbour.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a water taxi from the harbour reaches them in minutes — no need for an organised tour.

attractions.name: Hvar's lavender fields
attractions.text: Genuinely a real island industry, not just a photo prop, with purple fields scenting the island's interior each summer.
attractions.tip: Genuinely visit in late June or early July, when the lavender is in full, fragrant bloom.

attractions.name: Stari Grad

image.alt: The harbour of Stari Grad on Hvar island

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the oldest towns in Europe, its surrounding UNESCO-listed agricultural plain still farmed as it was in ancient Greek times.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a quieter, more low-key alternative base to Hvar Town itself.

attractions.name: The view from Fortica

image.alt: A panoramic view over Hvar Town and the Pakleni Islands

attractions.text: Genuinely one of Dalmatia's best panoramas, the harbour town and islands laid out together below.
attractions.tip: Genuinely bring a camera with a wide lens — the view sweeps across the whole coastline.

thingsToDoIntro: Hvar genuinely rewards splitting time between the harbour's energy and the quieter islands and countryside beyond it.

thingsToDo.title: Climb up to Fortica Španjola

image.alt: Climbing to Fortica Španjola above Hvar Town

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential walk, climbing through the old town's back lanes to the fortress and its panoramic view.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely go earlier in the day if you'd rather avoid the steepest part of the climb in full heat.

thingsToDo.title: Boat to the Pakleni Islands

image.alt: Boating to the Pakleni Islands near Hvar

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential half or full day, swimming and relaxing on the quieter islets just offshore.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely pack your own snacks and water if visiting a quieter cove without beach bars.

thingsToDo.title: Wander St Stephen's Square

image.alt: St Stephen's Square in Hvar Town

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to spend an hour, taking in the square's cathedral, arsenal and café terraces.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a good spot to get your bearings before exploring the town's smaller side streets.

thingsToDo.title: Visit the lavender fields in bloom

image.alt: Lavender fields in bloom on Hvar

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely fragrant, photogenic detour into the island's interior, best timed for peak bloom.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely rent a scooter or join a small tour to reach the fields easily from town.

thingsToDo.title: Day-trip to Stari Grad

image.alt: Stari Grad, one of Europe's oldest towns

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely worthwhile change of pace, exploring one of Europe's oldest continuously inhabited towns.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely an easy bus ride across the island from Hvar Town.

thingsToDo.title: Watch sunset from the harbour
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential evening ritual, the harbour glowing as yachts and day-trip boats return for the night.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely grab a waterfront table well before sunset in peak season, when the best spots fill early.

foodIntro: Hvar's food genuinely spans classic Dalmatian seafood alongside the island's own respected wine.

foods.name: Fresh grilled seafood

image.alt: Grilled seafood at a traditional Croatian restaurant

foods.text: Genuinely a highlight of dining here, fish and shellfish grilled simply at harbourfront konobas.
foods.whereToTry: Konobas throughout Hvar Town's harbour and back streets.

foods.name: Hvar wine (Plavac Mali)
foods.text: Genuinely a real point of local pride, bold red wines grown on the island's sun-soaked southern slopes.
foods.whereToTry: Wine bars and konobas throughout Hvar Town.

foods.name: Gregada (Hvar fish stew)
foods.text: Genuinely a distinctive island specialty, a simple stew of fish, potatoes and white wine cooked slowly together.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional konobas away from the busiest harbourfront strip.

foods.name: Dalmatinski pršut (dry-cured ham)
foods.text: Genuinely a reliable starter, often served with local cheese and olives.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants and konobas throughout Hvar Town.

foods.name: Crni rižot (black risotto)

image.alt: Black risotto made with cuttlefish ink

foods.text: Genuinely a Dalmatian classic, worth trying at least once during a Hvar visit.

foods.name: Fritule (small fried doughnuts)
foods.text: Genuinely a nice sweet treat, found at bakeries and market stalls around town.

accommodation.intro: Hvar genuinely runs from budget guesthouses to some of Croatia's most exclusive hotels, with prices climbing steeply in peak season.

areas.name: Hvar Town
areas.bestFor: Being genuinely in the middle of the island's nightlife and restaurant scene
areas.text: The most convenient, liveliest base, though also the priciest and busiest.

areas.name: Stari Grad
areas.bestFor: A genuinely quieter, more low-key stay
areas.text: A short bus ride from Hvar Town, with noticeably better value accommodation.

gettingThere.intro: Hvar is genuinely reached by sea, with no airport of its own on the island.

options.text: Genuinely the most common route, with frequent daily sailings in summer.
options.detail: The fast catamaran takes about an hour; the car ferry to Stari Grad takes around two.

options.text: Genuinely a longer but scenic option, sometimes with a change.
options.detail: Seasonal routes run more frequently in summer than winter.

options.text: Genuinely a flexible, if pricier, option from Split.
options.detail: Widely available through hotels and private operators.

gettingAround.intro: Hvar Town's genuinely car-free centre is entirely walkable, with boats and buses covering the rest of the island.

options.text: Genuinely the only way to explore Hvar Town's old streets.
options.detail: The harbour, square and fortress all sit within a comfortable walk of each other.

options.text: Genuinely the standard way to reach the Pakleni Islands.
options.detail: Frequent, inexpensive departures from the harbour throughout the day.

options.mode: Scooter or bus to Stari Grad and beyond
options.text: Genuinely useful for reaching the lavender fields and other towns.
options.detail: A scooter offers the most flexibility for exploring the island's interior.

bestTime.headline: Late June and September for lavender bloom and thinner crowds
bestTime.summary: Hvar is genuinely at its busiest and most expensive in July and August, with late June and September offering a better balance.

seasons.text: Genuinely warm enough to swim, with lavender fields at their fragrant best in late June.
Genuinely hot and lively, though Hvar Town gets genuinely crowded and prices peak.
Genuinely still warm enough for the sea, with crowds and prices both easing off noticeably.
Genuinely very quiet, with much of the island's hospitality scene closed for the season.

bestTime.avoid: Genuinely deep winter, when most restaurants and hotels close until spring.

itinerary.intro: Built around Hvar Town's essential sights and a full day on the Pakleni Islands.

days.title: Hvar Town and Fortica
days.summary: The harbour town and its hilltop fortress.
days.morning: St Stephen's Square and the harbour.
days.evening: Sunset views and dinner in the harbour.

days.title: The Pakleni Islands
days.summary: A full day on the water.
days.morning: Water taxi out to the Pakleni Islands.
days.afternoon: Swim and relax on a quiet cove.
days.evening: A final dinner back in Hvar Town.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Hvar visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book genuinely ferry and catamaran tickets ahead for peak summer sailings.
Book genuinely accommodation well ahead — Hvar Town genuinely sells out early in July and August.
Pack genuinely water shoes — many of the island's best coves are pebbly or rocky rather than sandy.
Visit genuinely in late June for the lavender fields at their fragrant, photogenic best.
Escape genuinely to the Pakleni Islands when Hvar Town's harbour feels too crowded.
Consider genuinely Stari Grad for better-value accommodation a short bus ride from the action.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Hvar?
faq.a: Two to three days genuinely covers Hvar Town, Fortica and a day on the Pakleni Islands comfortably.

faq.q: How do you get to Hvar?
faq.a: Genuinely by ferry or catamaran from Split, taking one to two hours depending on the service.
Genuinely one of Croatia's pricier islands, especially in July and August, when it draws a notably glamorous crowd.

faq.q: When do the lavender fields bloom?
faq.a: Genuinely late June into early July is the classic window, when the island's fields are at their most fragrant.

faq.q: Do you need a car on Hvar?
faq.a: No, genuinely not for Hvar Town itself, though a scooter or bus helps for reaching Stari Grad and the lavender fields.

faq.q: How does Hvar compare to Korčula?
faq.a: Genuinely livelier and more upscale — Korčula offers a quieter, more low-key version of a similar Dalmatian island experience.
